newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Japan zinc treatment deals seen aiding mines.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Japan zinc treatment deals seen aiding mines.

text.p: Pasminco Ltd, the world's largest zinc producer, is close to reaching final agreement on 1997/98 zinc concentrate treatment charges with the Japanese smelters after a series of industry settlements which improve producer terms, sources close to the talks said.
The remaining outstanding issue between Pasminco and the Japanese involves price escalator and de-escalator charges linked to the basis price, the sources said.
Terms are expected to be in line with those reached last month between MIM Holdings Ltd and the Japanese of around US$170.00 a tonne basis London Metal Exchange price of US$1,000 a tonne.

But they will also follow a weekend agreement reached in Australia between Normandy Mining Ltd's Western Australian mine Golden Grove and the Japanese smelters, which further improve terms for producers.
Pasminco hopes to have its talks finalised later this week.
"The full settlement is very close," the source said.
"All that's left are a few points regarding escalators and de-escalators."
Escalator and de-escalator charges can significantly affect the real price that smelters receive under contract terms.
In MIM's agreement, every $1.00 increase in the price increases the overall treatment charge by 16 cents up to a basis price of $1,100.
Beyond that the increase is 19 cents to a price of $1,450.
Several sources have confirmed that Normandy's Golden Grove had settled with Japanese zinc smelters for smaller tonnages than MIM and Pasminco will ship to Japan in the coming year.
Golden Grove's settlement is for 40,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates with treatment charges set at $185.00 a tonne on an LME price of $1,100 a tonne.
At surface-level this appears to be $1.00 less than Canadian miner Cominco Ltd's deal last month with French-based Metaleurop SA, but in fact was very similar to it, the sources said.
The Metaleurop agreement, commonly reported as $186.00, in fact involved two charges, one at A$185.00 for Red Dog concentrates and one at $187 for Polaris concentrates the sources said.
The Golden Grove agreement involves an escalator of 20 cents a dollar up to $1,350 and a de-escalator of 15 cents per dollar, sources said.
The significance of the Golden Grove agreement was that the up-scale above $1,350.00 was less than in the MIM agreement, setting better terms for producers than the MIM agreement, the sources noted.
Sources also noted that while miners negotiated improved terms from the Japanese this year, it was off a very low base.
The general improvement for miners is indicated by a decline in benchmark treatment charges, to $170 from $190 at a price of $1,000.
Other metal industry sources contacted by Reuters said that with zinc concentrates becoming much tighter, the smelters were losing their grip on ther market.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
